key_insight: An explainable ML workflow combining SHAP, permutation importance, and SR-KAN symbolic regression can recover a closed-form inductance formula that generalizes far better than standard black-box models.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, accurate self-inductance estimation for multilayer planar windings, reducing reliance on costly FEA or rigid hand-derived equations in high-frequency power converter design.
method: Built an open-source FEA dataset with 10,000+ simulations spanning seven OOD test classes.
Used feature attribution methods to interpret which geometric variables matter most.
Applied KAN-guided symbolic regression to discover an analytical inductance expression without preset formula structure.
evidence_signal: Across 55 PCB prototypes and 10,000+ FEA cases, the SR-KAN expression achieved 8.22% OOD relative error on simulations and 6.26% mean absolute relative error on hardware, while tree ensembles exceeded 36% OOD error.
watch_item: The learned formula is still data-dependent, so accuracy may drop for winding geometries or operating conditions outside the released dataset and validated prototype range.
paper_title: Explainable Machine Learning for Multilayer Planar Winding Inductance Estimation
